item.title: CollaFuse: Collaborative Diffusion Models
item.headline: Sharing image generation creates a trade-off between local work and information exposure
item.authors: Simeon Allmendinger, Domenique Zipperling, Lukas Struppek, and Niklas Kühl
item.summary: Splitting image denoising between server and clients improved fidelity over independently trained clients in tested settings. Privacy benefits were attack-specific, not guaranteed.

evidence.question: Can clients share generation work while retaining local specialization?
evidence.method: Five simulated clients; DDPM, Imagen, and latent-diffusion models on CIFAR-10, CelebA, and Animals-with-Attributes2; independent and pooled baselines.

explainer.finding: More server work favored image fidelity; more local work reduced leakage in the tested attacks.
explainer.method: Researchers varied where denoising changed hands, measuring image quality, attribute inference, and reconstruction attacks.
explainer.meaning: A server can start generating an image that a local model finishes. Moving that handoff changes both local effort and what shared intermediate images reveal.
explainer.limits: The system assumes an honest server and trustworthy training participants. Tested attacks do not establish formal privacy; malicious training and stronger adversaries remain concerns.
